subject: Stellaris-Lite integration: provisional hold and tokenization edgecases
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Caroline Park <caroline@nebula.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stellaris-Lite integration: provisional hold and tokenization edgecases

Team —

Nebula is asking us to onboard their Stellaris-Lite (3B) variant this sprint so they can run workloads in our Dedicated sandbox next month. Before we greenlight ingestion, I want a provisional hold (no public rollout / no pinned production variant) until we validate a short compatibility checklist. Two immediate concerns they surfaced:

- Tokenizer differences: Stellaris occasionally emits multi-byte control tokens for proprietary separators; this caused truncation in one internal test.
- KV cache alignment: their cache layout may require a different positional embedding handling in the runtime.

I attached token samples and a compatibility matrix Nebula provided. Can you comment on what minimal checks we need to sign off for a provisional onboard (not production pin) versus a full pin? Specifically:

1) David — runtime acceptance criteria (batching, kv alignment tests, max-seq behavior).
2) Laura — product/console impacts (routing/fallback behavior if variant is not pinned).
3) Priyom — QA/ML evals we should run (tokenization drift, generation shift, eval harness).

Proposed quick path: 48–72h triage -> canary on Dedicated sandbox -> pin request only if pass. If any of you think the risk is higher, flag it here and we'll escalate with Legal/Security.

Attachments: stellaris_token_samples.json, compatibility_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov | Lead PM, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Caroline Park <caroline@nebula.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris-Lite integration: provisional hold and tokenization edgecases

Olga —

Thanks for the heads-up and the samples. Quick read-through and my initial runbook:

- Tokenization: we'll convert their token samples into our token-map and run the tokenizer round-trip test (input -> tokens -> decode) across 5k examples. If >0.5% of sequences fail (mismatch or decode error) we block.
- KV cache alignment: add a positional alignment test to the KV replay harness. If their layout requires custom offsets we'll need a micro-patch in the KV manager; estimate 1-2 dev days.
- Batching/latency: run our continuous-batcher with their model in a sandbox profile (seq len 512 / burst traffic). If tail P95 latency increases by >25% under the same throughput, we treat as a regression and require optimization.

I can spin up the sandbox tests Monday morning and have a first-pass report by EOD Monday (2026-08-31). If we need a runtime patch, we should plan a short freeze window for the Dedicated pool pinning.

For now I support a provisional hold until tests complete.

-David
David Kim | Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Caroline Park <caroline@nebula.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris-Lite integration: provisional hold and tokenization edgecases

Thanks David / Olga —

Small add from product/console side:

- Routing & fallback: If we keep the variant unpinned in production, we must ensure requests from Nebula's account route to a quarantined pool (Dedicated sandbox) only. That is already possible with an ingress policy, but we need the MLP (mutual action plan) updated to reflect 'no global routing' until pin approval.
- Observability: Add a temporary dashboard (per-route tokens, tokenization error rate, kv-cache misses, P95 latency) so the CS contact at Nebula can see progress. Priyom — can you add the tokenization drift eval to the quality dashboard and surface a pass/fail metric?
- Legal note: If their tokenizer uses proprietary separator bytes, we should confirm there are no IP concerns before embedding adaptors. I'll loop in Legal if needed, but want to avoid a full legal review unless we see code reuse.

Timeline suggestion:
- 2026-08-31: runtime & tokenization tests complete (David + Priyom)
- 2026-09-01: dedicated sandbox canary + observability dashboard up (Laura + David)
- 2026-09-02: internal review and pin decision meeting (PM + Runtime + ML + CS)

If everyone agrees, I'll update the intake ticket and the MLP doc (link below) and mark this as provisional hold until the meeting.

MLP draft: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c_stellaris_integration_notes

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Director, Product — Redwood Console
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Caroline Park <caroline@nebula.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris-Lite integration: provisional hold and tokenization edgecases

Looping back after a quick pass on the token samples and a small eval run:

- Tokenization drift: initial 2k sample roundtrip shows 0.18% decode anomalies concentrated on a proprietary separator token. That's below the 0.5% threshold David proposed but I want a second run with a different sample set (we requested a fuller dump from Nebula).
- Quality regressions: generation on 500 prompt seeds showed negligible semantic drift; however, the separator token changes a small number of scores in completion boundaries (affects snippet extraction).

Canary proposal:
- Enable variant in Dedicated sandbox only (no global routing).
- Run a 48h canary with synthetic traffic at 50rps and the Nebula test suite.
- Dashboard pass conditions: tokenization error rate <0.5%, stable P95 latency, no more than 0.2% of completions with boundary truncation.

If canary passes, request: pin Stellaris-Lite as "stellaris-lite-v1.1-provisional" in Dedicated for an initial 30-day observation window before any public routing. Laura/Olga: please confirm the MLP entry and I will attach the eval report.

-attached: canary_runbook.md

Priyom Das | Applied ML Engineer, Model Quality
